title: although, though, even though; in spite of, despite
subtitle: although it rained / in spite of the rain / despite the rain
summary: Use although (or though / even though) with a subject and verb, and in spite of / despite with a noun, pronoun or -ing, to contrast two ideas.

lesson.heading: Study this situation
lesson.text: Last year Paul and Sarah had a holiday by the sea. It rained a lot, but they had a good time. You can say this with **although** + a clause, or with **in spite of / despite** + a noun.

examples.text: **Although** it rained a lot, they had a good time.
examples.note: = It rained a lot, but they ...

examples.text: **In spite of** the rain, they had a good time.
**Despite** the rain, they had a good time.

left.label: although + subject + verb
left.text: After although we use a subject + verb. Although introduces a contrast.
examples: **Although** it rained a lot, they had a good time.
I didn't apply for the job **although** I had the necessary qualifications.
We went out **although** it was raining heavily.

right.label: because + subject + verb
examples: We didn't go out **because** it was raining heavily.

lesson.heading: in spite of / despite
lesson.text: After **in spite of** or **despite**, we use a noun, a pronoun (this / that / what etc.) or -ing. Despite is the same as in spite of. We say in spite of, but despite (without of). You can also say **in spite of the fact (that) ...** and **despite the fact (that) ...**. Compare in spite of (contrast) and because of (reason).

examples.text: **In spite of** the rain, we had a good time.
She wasn't well, but **in spite of this** she continued working.
**In spite of what** I said yesterday, I still love you.
I didn't apply for the job **in spite of having** the necessary qualifications.
She wasn't well, but **despite this** she continued working.
I didn't apply for the job **despite the fact that** I had the necessary qualifications.
We went out **in spite of** the rain. / We didn't go out **because of** the rain.

lesson.heading: although or in spite of / despite?

left.label: although + clause
examples: **Although** the traffic was bad, we arrived on time.
I couldn't sleep **although** I was very tired.

right.label: in spite of / despite + noun or -ing
examples: **In spite of** the traffic, we arrived on time. (not in spite of the traffic was bad)
I couldn't sleep **despite** being very tired. (not despite I was tired)

lesson.heading: though and even though
lesson.text: **Though** = although. In spoken English we often use though at the end of a sentence, where it means 'but'. **Even though** (but not 'even' alone) is similar to although.

examples.text: I didn't apply for the job **though** I had the necessary qualifications.
The house isn't so nice. I like the garden **though**.
I see them every day. I've never spoken to them **though**.
examples.note: = but I've never spoken to them

examples.text: **Even though** I was really tired, I couldn't sleep.

lesson.text: Look at what follows: a subject + verb needs although / though / even though; a noun, pronoun or -ing needs in spite of / despite. And it is always despite, never ~~despite of~~.

exercises.prompt: ___ it rained a lot, we had a good time.
exercises.explanation: There is a subject + verb (it rained), and the sentence is a contrast, so: Although.

exercises.prompt: ___ all our careful plans, a lot of things went wrong.
exercises.explanation: A noun phrase (all our careful plans) and a contrast: In spite of (or Despite).

exercises.prompt: Complete each sentence with the right although-clause.

pairs.right: although she has a very important job.

pairs.left: I recognised her from a photo,
pairs.right: although I had never seen her before.

pairs.left: We decided to invite them to the party,
pairs.right: although we don't like them very much.

pairs.left: I managed to make myself understood,
pairs.right: although I didn't speak the language well.

exercises.prompt: I went to work the next day ___ I was still feeling unwell.
exercises.explanation: A contrast followed by subject + verb (I was feeling): although.

exercises.prompt: Sam accepted the job ___ the salary, which was rather low.
exercises.explanation: A noun (the salary) and a contrast (the salary was low, but he accepted): in spite of (or despite).

exercises.prompt: Which words can follow each group? Sort the endings.

exercises.explanation: After despite we use -ing, not a subject + verb: despite being very tired.

exercises.prompt: We live in the same building, but we hardly ever see each other. ___ in the same building, we hardly ever see each other.
exercises.explanation: Despite + -ing: Despite living in the same building.

exercises.prompt: We played quite well, but we lost the game. Make one sentence with in spite of.
exercises.answer: In spite of playing quite well, we lost the game.
exercises.explanation: In spite of + -ing (playing) introduces the contrast.

exercises.prompt: They hadn't been invited, but they came to the party. Make one sentence with even though.
exercises.answer: They came to the party even though they hadn't been invited.
alternatives: Even though they hadn't been invited, they came to the party.
exercises.explanation: Even though + subject + verb (they hadn't been invited).

exercises.statement: She wasn't well, but despite of this she continued working.
exercises.explanation: She wasn't well, but despite this she continued working. We say in spite of, but despite (without of).

exercises.statement: Even I was really tired, I couldn't sleep.
exercises.explanation: Even though I was really tired, I couldn't sleep. Even alone cannot introduce a clause.

exercises.statement: I see them every day. I've never spoken to them though.
exercises.explanation: Correct. In spoken English, though at the end of a sentence means 'but'.

exercises.prompt: Laura is very nice. I ___ though.
exercises.explanation: Though at the end of the sentence = but: I don't like her husband though.
